bare-string-params.describes: share of parameters declared as a bare string rather than a domain type
bare-string-params.remedy: Introduce a newtype for the concept. Three interchangeable strings in one signature is an argument swap that still compiles and still runs.

broad-lint-silencing.describes: crate-wide allow(clippy::all) or allow(warnings), per 10k lines
broad-lint-silencing.remedy: Replace the blanket allow with the specific lints meant, or fix them. A crate-wide allow also silences everything written after it, including code nobody has typed yet.

crate-type-scatter.describes: crates whose signatures are mostly built from three or more other crates' types
crate-type-scatter.remedy: A crate built mostly from other crates' types, pulled from several of them, usually wants splitting or absorbing. One strong pull is an adapter and perfectly fine.

default-allow-dispatch.describes: a dispatch that checks in its arms and does nothing in its catch-all, per 10k lines
default-allow-dispatch.remedy: Match the action exhaustively, with no catch-all, so a new action cannot be added without deciding what it is allowed to do. As written, everything nobody listed is permitted.

discarded-check.describes: a permission or validation call whose answer is thrown away, per 10k lines
discarded-check.remedy: Handle the result. `let _ = enforce_read(path)` reads as enforcement at a glance and performs none — it is worse than no call at all, because a reviewer counts it.

duplicated-bodies.describes: function bodies that are exact token copies of another, per 10k lines
duplicated-bodies.remedy: Move the shared body somewhere both callers can reach. The copies are listed below; they were found by exact token match, so they were copied rather than merely similar.

env-controlled-spawn.describes: spawn targets chosen by an environment variable, per 10k lines
env-controlled-spawn.remedy: Resolve the program from a known location, or validate it before spawning. As it stands, whoever sets the variable chooses what runs.

exit-in-library.describes: process::exit called from a library crate, per 10k lines
exit-in-library.remedy: Return an error and let the binary decide the exit code. A library that exits takes that decision away from every caller, including a test harness.

hand-built-json.describes: JSON assembled by interpolation rather than serialised, per 10k lines
hand-built-json.remedy: Serialise with serde. A value interpolated into a format string decides the structure around it, which is the same mistake as building SQL by concatenation.

oversized-files.describes: files longer than max_lines, per 10k lines — a house standard, not a fact
oversized-files.remedy: Split the file, or raise the standard if this is simply how the project is written: cqx config set oversized-files.max_lines N. Measured across ripgrep, tokio and deno, file length tracks habit rather than quality.

oversized-line-share.describes: share of all lines living in files longer than max_lines
oversized-line-share.remedy: Same standard as oversized-files, measured by weight rather than count: it catches a codebase where most of the code lives in a handful of very large files.

permission-granting-argument.describes: a subprocess handed a literal argument that relaxes its own checks, per 10k lines
permission-granting-argument.remedy: Forward the caller's policy instead of overriding it. A child spawned with the permission checks turned off does not inherit the parent's answer, it discards it.

result-string-density.describes: functions returning Result<_, String> instead of a real error type, per 10k lines
result-string-density.remedy: Give the crate an error type and return that. A String error cannot be matched on, so every caller either re-parses the text or swallows it.

shell-argument-unchecked.describes: a shell handed an argument the extractor could not resolve, per 10k lines
shell-argument-unchecked.remedy: Check every program the script invokes, not only the first word, or refuse anything but a single command. Validating the head of a string and running the whole of it through a shell means `git status; rm -rf ~` passes a check for `git`.

shell-invocation.describes: spawning a shell, which turns an argument into a command, per 10k lines
shell-invocation.remedy: Pass the program and its arguments directly rather than through a shell. A shell turns an argument into a command.

typescript/any-density.describes: explicit TypeScript any annotations and assertions, per 10k lines
typescript/any-density.remedy: Use unknown and narrow it, or give the value its domain type.

typescript/duplicated-bodies.describes: function bodies that are exact token copies of another, per 10k lines
typescript/duplicated-bodies.remedy: Move the shared body somewhere both callers can reach. The copies are listed below; they were found by exact token match, so they were copied rather than merely similar.

typescript/dynamic-code.describes: global eval/Function calls and literal-string timers, per 10k lines
typescript/dynamic-code.remedy: Use ordinary functions and pass a callback to timers instead of executing strings.

typescript/dynamic-html.describes: non-literal HTML at raw HTML sinks, per 10k lines
typescript/dynamic-html.remedy: Use textContent or JSX text. Review sanitization if raw HTML is intentional; this syntax rule cannot prove a sanitizer's contract.

typescript/exit-in-library.describes: global process.exit outside a bin or explicit entry file, per 10k lines
typescript/exit-in-library.remedy: Return an error and let the entry point choose the process exit code.

typescript/oversized-files.describes: files longer than max_lines, per 10k lines — a house standard, not a fact
typescript/oversized-files.remedy: Split the file, or set typescript/oversized-files.params.max_lines in cqx.json to the project's standard.

typescript/oversized-line-share.describes: share of all lines living in files longer than max_lines
typescript/oversized-line-share.remedy: Same standard as oversized-files, measured by weight rather than count: it catches a codebase where most of the code lives in a handful of very large files.

typescript/swallowed-errors.describes: empty catches without an explanation, per 10k lines
typescript/swallowed-errors.remedy: Handle or rethrow the error, or explain in the catch why ignoring it is safe.

typescript/undocumented-suppressions.describes: @ts-ignore or eslint-disable comments without a reason, per 10k lines
typescript/undocumented-suppressions.remedy: Add a reason after @ts-ignore, or an ESLint -- description.

unbounded-send-sync.describes: unsafe impl Send/Sync for a generic type with no thread-safety bound, per 10k lines
unbounded-send-sync.remedy: Add the bound the promise depends on: `unsafe impl<T: Send> Sync for Holder<T>`. Without it the type claims every `T` is safe to share, including an `Rc`. This shape accounts for sixteen of sixty-five RustSec advisories sampled — and tokio writes it twenty-three times deliberately, which is why this rule is off until you turn it on: cqx config enable unbounded-send-sync.

undocumented-suppressions.describes: crate-level lint suppressions with no reason given, per 10k lines
undocumented-suppressions.remedy: Add reason = "..." to each suppression. deno documents every one of its crate-level suppressions, which is why theirs read as decisions rather than residue.

unproven-spawn-targets.describes: share of spawn and env targets the extractor could not resolve
unproven-spawn-targets.remedy: Where the target comes from a parameter, the caller is deciding it — hoisting the spawn there makes it knowable. Where it comes from the environment, that is the finding rather than a gap.
